title: 🎨 Visual Canon & Reference Collection
rawNotionMarkup:
This page preserves visual continuity for Eryndor's characters, locations, creatures, weapons, maps and future video scenes. Character faces and distinctive traits should remain recognisable as the story advances; clothing, equipment, injuries, age and status may change through events.

## Gloin — primary portrait reference

The user approved a regenerated portrait as the primary reference. Established visual traits:

- Rugged young adult dwarf.
- Reddish-brown long hair and blue-grey eyes.
- Strong facial features.
- Braided, ringed beard.

The portrait also depicts practical leather and metal gear, a fur-lined cloak, a mountain rune clasp, a rune-etched axe and a round shield with a mountain emblem. These are visible in the portrait but do not lock Gloin's future outfit, weapons or equipment. His appearance should remain consistent unless the user changes it or events visibly alter it.

## Maela Deepforge — visual reference

- Female Khazari master runesmith.
- Silver-grey hair tightly braided back.
- Small metal rings in the braids.
- Her clothing is not fixed.

## Borin Ashmantle — visual reference notes

- Older dwarf.
- Grey beard.

- Other fine visual details remain open unless separately established.

## Hadrik Ironvein — visual reference notes

- Khazari scholar.
- Greying hair has been suggested, but its exact colour and style are not firmly established.

## Visual production rules

- ChatGPT generates still images for Eryndor.
- fal is reserved exclusively for video generation.
- Use established still images as references for consistency when making videos.
- Prefer individual portraits and assets over collages.
- Rebuild older visuals as individual assets when needed; do not claim an asset exists unless it has actually been generated and retained.
- Track visual canon separately from temporary clothing and equipment.
- Do not save an image to a persistent reference collection unless the user explicitly asks or approves.

## Canon boundaries

- A portrait is a visual reference, not automatic proof of equipment ownership, skill, status or biography.
- Clothing and carried equipment can change through play; do not force a character to retain items merely because they appeared in a portrait.
- Preserve the distinction between approved visual traits and details that are merely suggested or not yet established.
- Do not invent precise visual traits for characters whose references are incomplete.
